topic: Doflamingo's second chance for Bellamy in Dressrosa was a setup because Dellinger was already sent to remove him
title: Bellamy's Second Chance Was A Setup
description: Bellamy got a second chance to become a Donquixote Pirates officer in Dressrosa, but Dellinger was already waiting with the real order. Here is why that mission looks like a trap. Was Doflamingo ever going to let him succeed?
comment: Did Doflamingo send Bellamy after Luffy hoping he'd win, or was the mission always a way to get rid of him? Pick one.

lines.text: Bellamy's second chance in Dressrosa was never a chance. Doflamingo had already written him off.

shot.fallback: pirate nervously facing a grinning feather-coated boss

lines.text: He hands Doflamingo a gold pillar as a declaration of loyalty.

shot.fallback: pirate presenting a tall golden pillar to his boss

lines.text: He loses the tournament, so he gets one more shot: take Luffy down.

shot.fallback: pirate receiving an order from a grinning boss

lines.text: Here's what most people missed. Doflamingo expects him to fail again.

shot.fallback: small cheerful fighter blocking a pirate's path

lines.text: Bellamy walks up to Luffy, and Dellinger arrives with orders to remove him.

shot.fallback: small fighter stopping a pirate in a corridor

lines.text: In chapter 731, Dellinger beats him badly until Bartolomeo's barrier steps in.

shot.fallback: green-haired fan shielding a pirate with a barrier

lines.text: My read is that the mission was never a test. It was a loose end with Luffy as the excuse.

shot.fallback: scheming warlord watching a pirate from a balcony

lines.text: People say Doflamingo wanted Luffy gone either way. But why send a man he'd already marked?

shot.fallback: grinning warlord with sunglasses in a palace

lines.text: Because a failure gave him a reason to act, and a win handed him a free victory.

shot.fallback: warlord's silhouette behind a pirate in a dim hall

lines.text: But what Bellamy does once he learns the truth is the part nobody expected.
And all of it tells you why Bellamy's second chance in Dressrosa was never a chance...

shot.fallback: pirate beside a golden pillar looking uneasy

self_check.hook: Contrarian claim in line 1 about the second chance being a setup
